subject: Cooking
title: Radiation: The Invisible Heat of Grilling
description: Learn Radiation: The Invisible Heat of Grilling in one minute.

hook.text: Hold your hand above a grill and you feel heat without touching anything. That's radiation.

buildup.text: Infrared radiation travels as electromagnetic waves — no contact or air movement needed.

discovery.text: A broiler cooks purely by radiation, blasting food with infrared from above at 500°F+.

twist.text: Dark surfaces absorb more radiation than shiny ones — black pans brown faster than silver.

climax.text: This is why toast browns on top under a broiler but stays pale on the bottom.

punchline.text: Grilling is cooking with invisible light.

quiz.question: What type of energy transfer cooks food under a broiler?

details.summary: Infrared radiation transfers heat through electromagnetic waves without needing contact or a medium. Glowing charcoal, broiler elements, and campfires all cook by radiating infrared energy directly to food surfaces. Radiation intensity drops with the square of distance from the heat source.
details.whyItMatters: Radiation explains why grilling and broiling create intense surface browning. Managing distance from the heat source is the key to controlling radiant cooking.
takeaways: Infrared radiation heats food without physical contact
Heat intensity decreases rapidly with distance from source
Dark surfaces absorb more radiant energy than shiny ones

faq.question: Why does charcoal grilling taste different from gas?
faq.answer: Charcoal emits more infrared radiation at higher intensity, creating stronger Maillard reactions on the surface. Fat drippings vaporize on coals and rise as flavorful smoke. Gas grills produce less radiant heat and fewer smoke compounds, resulting in milder flavor.

faq.question: How does distance from heat affect grilling?
faq.answer: Radiant energy follows the inverse square law — doubling the distance reduces heat to one quarter. Raising the grill grate even slightly changes cooking intensity dramatically. This is why adjustable grate height gives you precise control over sear versus gentle cooking.
